summary: The first 300 mm line built under a December 2017 agreement between Silan and Xiamen Semiconductor Investment Group in Xiamen's Haicang District, run by a joint project company in which the state-owned Xiamen group holds the majority and Silan about 27%. Planned at CNY 7 billion and 80,000 wafers a month at 90nm over two phases, it was connected in 2020 and entered formal production in December 2020. It reached its Phase 1 target of 40,000 wafers a month by the end of 2021, when Phase 2 was already under way, and it makes trench, shielded-gate and superjunction MOSFETs, IGBTs and high-voltage ICs. Silan reported the line running at full load in 2025 and the first half of 2026, with output of 637,400 wafers in 2025.

location.note: The line is in Haicang District; the operator's registered address is 89 Lanying Road, Haicang District.

notes: The 2017 agreement also foresaw a second 300 mm line as a third phase (65nm to 90nm, about CNY 10 billion, details to be agreed). Silan's 2025 annual report and 2026 interim report list a Silan Jike 300 mm power-chip line phase 3 project under way to add automotive analog, IGBT and MOSFET capacity, but give no investment, capacity, site or dates and do not say whether it is that second line; it is not part of this record, and the 2026 interim report lists it as a separate project from Silan Jihua's 300 mm analog line (existing record china-silan-xiamen-12-inch-analog). Silan reported annual output of 470,000 wafers in 2022 and 464,000 in 2023, IGBT capacity of 25,000 wafers a month by the end of 2023, and 394,500 wafers in the first half of 2026. The project company had revenue of about CNY 3.19 billion in 2025 and reported net losses for 2023, 2024 and 2025 (about CNY 57 million in 2025) before a net profit of about CNY 93 million in the first half of 2026. Sources read here do not report a completion date for Phase 2. In March 2026 the company sought a 12-year CNY 300 million project loan from China Development Bank's Xiamen branch.
